reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to Gauss’s theory of least squares and Quetelet’s application of the 'average man' to social physics. Francis Galton later operationalized these concepts to study heredity, explicitly linking the normal curve of error to biological regression. The historical pivot occurred when probabilistic thinking shifted from celestial mechanics to terrestrial biology, establishing the foundation for modern quantitative genetics and, by extension, contemporary predictive analytics in human performance domains.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires viewing selection pressures—such as 'Marriage Selection in respect to Eye Colour' (Quote 10)—as adversarial optimization problems. One agent (nature/environment) seeks to maximize entropy and regression to the mean, while the opposing agent (selection/breeding programs) attempts to minimize variance and lock in extreme phenotypes. Our primitives capture this tug-of-war by treating the probability integral as a dynamic battlefield where the expected value is constantly being pulled between the prior distribution and the observed likelihood.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent anti-collinearity and leakage between layers, we enforce a strict veto condition: if the empirical kurtosis of the observed dataset significantly deviates from the mesokurtic baseline of the Gaussian primitive, the operator must be suspended. This prevents the system from blindly applying linear regression kernels to fundamentally non-linear, chaotic regimes. Furthermore, any telemetry signal indicating a breakdown in the independence assumption—such as synchronized environmental shocks affecting multiple traits simultaneously—triggers a hard reset of the conformal prediction intervals, ensuring the integrity of the sovereign inference engine.
